title: VAD Boundary Finder
description: Voice activity detection finds where speech starts and ends inside a push-to-talk recording. The chapter's VAD is a four-state machine (SILENCE, STARTING, SPEECH, ENDING) driven by the hysteresis gate: 3 loud frames in a row start speech, 15 quiet frames in a row end it. The start is the first loud frame of that run and the end is the last loud frame, and the device keeps 4 frames of pre-roll and 5 of hang-over around them.

learningObjectives: The learner will execute the voice activity detection rules on 5 loudness traces to find each trace's first and last speech frame, matching both frames in at least 4 of 5 traces.
prerequisites: loudness in bits, frame, level gate, hysteresis, voice activity detection, start frames, end frames, state machine (all defined in this chapter above the block).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: Why is the start reported earlier than the frame at which it is signaled?
Why does a single loud click never start speech?
What is the end of a trace that is still loud at its last frame?
commonMisconceptions: (1) Speech starts at the frame where the VAD signals "start". (2) Any loud frame starts speech. (3) Any quiet frame ends speech. (4) A trace that is still loud at its last frame has no end.
assessmentOpportunities: Complete all five traces. Mastery is 4 of 5 traces fully correct on the first attempt.
